note: What this project produces that another project can consume, and what it currently consumes from others. Written so a reader does not have to reverse-engineer the repository to find out. Every 'measured' line is something that was run, with the date; every 'not-consumed' line is a real absence, not a plan.

produces.what: a zip that unpacks into a runner, a verifier and 58 cases
produces.how: curl the raw URL, unpack, `python run.py` in a clean directory
produces.measured: 2026-11-27: 389,203 bytes, sha256 a5c0e5b7...71ffc, 58/58 rc=0 on Windows and on Linux, anonymously fetched on both
produces.caveat: the archive is not byte-identical across operating systems: the same tree built on Linux gives 389,201 bytes / e57c052f...

produces.what: one JSON line per package, written by the verifier itself: vector, result, checks_failed, verifier identity, exit code
produces.where: uibc_core.pyz verify <pkg> --report <file.jsonl> --vector-id <id>, or uibc_core.pyz verify-dir <dir> --report <file.jsonl>; shape: interop/verify-report.schema.json (draft 2020-12); checker: tools/report_lint.py
produces.measured: 2026-11-27: six contracts in tests/test_verify_report.py; on Linux, 58 shipped cases produced 58 lines and 52 of them named the failing check; an unreadable input (a single statement file) produced one ERROR line with exit 3; 2026-11-27 (later): six schema contracts plus an optional jsonschema validation pass
produces.caveat: the line carries our verdict vocabulary and our check ids; a consumer still has to map both. Lines are appended, so a harness must not assume one line per file

produces.what: one JSON line per SCITT/COSE Transparent Statement: verdict, the named ground for a refusal, the observer position, and the verifier identity
produces.where: uibc_core.pyz verify-cose --manifest M --statements DIR --report <file.jsonl>; shape: interop/scitt-cose-report.schema.json; checker: tools/report_lint.py
produces.measured: 2026-11-27: on probityai/agent-evidence-vectors corpora/vectors-scitt-cose (27 members, corpusDigest 79d651d3...) 27/27 answers conform to the answers the corpus declares, judged at the instant its own witnesses use (1789041600 = 2026-09-10T12:00Z); at each vector's own verificationTime 26/27, and the one that differs is the expiry member, whose exp (1789038000) is after the verificationTime that file carries (1788955200) and before the corpus' witness clock
produces.caveat: 27/27 is a self-run of their published corpus with our own reader. Their rail has not been re-run against this build, so this is a measurement of our reading, not of their scoring

produces.what: a small aee-scitt-cose/v0.1 corpus of our own making: tag-18 COSE_Sign1 statements with CWT claims and RFC 9942 receipts, plus a manifest that lists them
produces.measured: 2026-11-27: emitted 3 statements over one Merkle tree (root 052d3ad994eb059c...199d), one of them carrying a detached payload; read back 3/3 valid by our own reader and 3/3 conforming in corpus mode
produces.caveat: the statements are produced and judged by the same project, and no foreign reader has been run against them; the emitter also only produces statements that should be valid, so it is not a corpus of refusals

produces.what: one JSON object per package: result, checks with ids, and the reason for each
produces.how: run the pyz with a Python 3 interpreter; stdout is the JSON, stderr is the explanation
produces.measured: 2026-11-27: on 58 shipped cases, and on 3 packages built by someone else, the verdict never disagreed with the expectation
produces.caveat: the verdict vocabulary is ours. A consumer expecting a boolean pass/fail has to map FAIL, INCONCLUSIVE and abstention onto its own scale, and that mapping is the consumer's claim, not ours

produces.what: the record a kit run leaves behind: verifier version, case count, passed count, and who ran it
produces.measured: 2026-11-27: run_by is null in anonymous runs, so a receipt written by the author and one written by a stranger are distinguishable

produces.what: the record of testing someone else's packages with our verifier
produces.measured: 2026-11-27: 58/58 against the shipped kit, and 3/3 against three packages written outside this project
produces.caveat: one person, one machine, one run. Not an audit, not a certification

produces.what: the per-action evidence layout the verifier reads: identity, lifecycle, manifest, evidence files, one digest chain
produces.caveat: documented at the file level, not as a normative specification with a versioned grammar

consumes.measured: 2026-11-28: on the peer corpus corpora/vectors-key-revocation-list at head 08f16c3 (13 members, corpusDigest f790ade4...e77) our reader matched the answer key on every decision and reason for 13/13, and on both declarations the manifest makes about each list - that the claimed signer thumbprint is the honest one, and that the signature verifies under the key the envelope carries. The five decisions are revoked, not_revoked, no_statement, rejected and stale, and the process exits 0/1/2/3/4 by them, because that is the contract the suite runs external verifiers under.
consumes.blocked_by: none for reading. Two states the reference reader answers by folding are refused here instead (an instant in a second spelling, and two records for one key that disagree); their harness has not been re-run against this build, so this is our reading of their files.

consumes.measured: 2026-11-28: on the peer corpus corpora/vectors-agent-card-receipt at head 08f16c3 (49 members: 13 accept, 36 reject, corpusDigest 4eab50c3...8e18) our reader matched the answer key on decision and reason for 49/49, across all sixteen reason tokens and the fifteen rules they are reached by. There is one accepting reason, receipt_current. The subject digest is recomputed here as SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 form of the card without its top-level signatures, excluding that member by its parsed name and once only, with numbers in ECMAScript form (0.93 and 1e-06 are ordinary, and the number form was checked against RFC 8785 Appendix B's table from the raw bits). A missing, malformed, foreign-signed or stale revocation list is a refusal and never a clean pass.
consumes.blocked_by: none for reading. Their harness has not been re-run against this build, so this is our reading of their files, not their scoring; and the A2A digest rule is read from the corpus' own statements, not from an A2A conformance run.

consumes.measured: 2026-11-28: on the peer corpus corpora/vectors-revocation-list at head 1ab5db7 (87 members: 9 accept, 78 reject, corpusDigest 87dfad7d...be95) our reader reproduced all five recorded fields - decision, the refused list's index, the reason as code:detail, the digests of every list up to the refused one, and the list in force at the verdict - for 87/87. Signatures are checked with this package's own Ed25519 verifier over RFC 8785 canonical bodies, and the chain is folded here rather than delegated to their harness.
consumes.blocked_by: none for reading the cumulative chain. The delta form (predicate/v2/revocation-list, deltas folded by sequence number and digest) is still unread, and their reference verifier has not been re-run against this build, so this is our reading of their files.

consumes.measured: 2026-11-27: 58/58 shipped cases, plus 3 foreign packages accepted or refused as their authors expected

2026-11-27: our verifier now reads tagged COSE_Sign1 (tag 18) with CWT claims, the private-use observer position (label -70001) and RFC 9942 receipts; on the peer corpus' 27 members it agreed with the declared answer 27/27 at the corpus' witness instant and 26/27 at each vector's own verificationTime; the reader re-derives the RFC 9162 inclusion root itself instead of sharing the corpus' tree code
consumes.blocked_by: none for reading. Remaining gap: their external rail has not run against this build, and their corpus' expiry member carries a verificationTime that contradicts its own declared verdict, which is recorded rather than smoothed over

consumes.measured: 2026-11-28: on the peer corpus corpora/vectors-mcp-authz at head 08f16c3 (11 members: 1 accept, 10 reject) our reader reached 11/11 by the corpus' own convention - verdict matches and at least one of the member's declared codes is named; no declared code was missed. Two members carry one extra code each, reported rather than suppressed. The corpus was the peer's, not ours: this is our reading of their files, not their harness re-running us.
